title: "Length-Outlier Exclusion vs. Per-Thread Subsampling"
output:
  bookdown::pdf_document2:
    toc: false
    latex_engine: xelatex
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)
library(stringr)
library(kableExtra)

rm(list = ls())
if (rstudioapi::isAvailable()) {
  setwd(dirname(rstudioapi::getActiveDocumentContext()$path))
}

# kableExtra 1.4.0 duplicates bookdown HTML caption numbers for tables piped
# through row_spec()/kable_styling() (github.com/haozhu233/kableExtra/issues/831);
# forcing format = "html" avoids it. PDF auto-detects "latex" and is unaffected.
html_fmt <- function() if (knitr::is_html_output()) "html" else NULL
shrink <- function(k) if (knitr::is_latex_output()) kable_styling(k, font_size = 8) else k

out_dir <- "../../output/5_inference_final"
overview <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "length_outlier_test_summary.csv"))
sf <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "length_outlier_test_shortfall_by_group.csv"))
nz <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "length_outlier_test_nonzero_by_group.csv"))

mechanism_names <- c(ER = "Emotional Reactions", IP = "Interpretations", EX = "Explorations")
rules_order <- c("none", "iqr_1.5_raw", "iqr_1.5_log", "iqr_3.0_log", "mad_3.5_log",
                 "percentile_1_99_log", "percentile_2.5_97.5_log")
rule_labels <- c(none = "None", iqr_1.5_raw = "IQR1.5 raw", iqr_1.5_log = "IQR1.5 log",
                 iqr_3.0_log = "IQR3 log", mad_3.5_log = "MAD3.5 log",
                 percentile_1_99_log = "P1-99 log", `percentile_2.5_97.5_log` = "P2.5-97.5 log")
chosen_rule <- "mad_3.5_log"

group_order <- as.vector(t(outer(c("Gemini", "Openai", "Grok"), c("DG", "SAG", "SAGII"),
                                 paste, sep = " / ")))
add_group <- function(d) d %>% mutate(group = paste(str_to_title(model), toupper(method), sep = " / "))
sf <- add_group(sf)
nz <- add_group(nz)

# Wide table: rows = (model, method) group plus a pooled row, columns = rules.
wide_table <- function(long, value, pooled) {
  w <- long %>% select(group, outlier_rule, all_of(value)) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = outlier_rule, values_from = all_of(value))
  w <- w[match(group_order, w$group), ]
  p <- pooled %>% pivot_wider(names_from = outlier_rule, values_from = pct) %>% mutate(group = "All synthetic")
  out <- bind_rows(w, p)[, c("group", rules_order)]
  colnames(out) <- c("Group", unname(rule_labels[rules_order]))
  out
}

pooled_sf <- sf %>% group_by(outlier_rule) %>%
  summarise(pct = 100 * sum(n_shortfall_cells) / sum(n_cells), .groups = "drop")
pooled_nz <- function(mech) nz %>% filter(mechanism == mech) %>% group_by(outlier_rule) %>%
  summarise(pct = 100 * sum(n_nonzero_excluded) / sum(n_nonzero), .groups = "drop")

pooled_range <- function(pooled) {
  r <- pooled %>% filter(outlier_rule != "none")
  lo <- r %>% slice_min(pct, n = 1); hi <- r %>% slice_max(pct, n = 1)
  sprintf("%.2f%% (%s) to %.2f%% (%s)", lo$pct, rule_labels[lo$outlier_rule], hi$pct, rule_labels[hi$outlier_rule])
}

worst_group <- function(long, value, rule) {
  w <- long %>% filter(outlier_rule == rule) %>% slice_max(.data[[value]], n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
  sprintf("%.2f%% (%s)", w[[value]], w$group)
}

n_zero_baseline <- sum(sf$n_shortfall_cells[sf$outlier_rule == "none"])

# Subsampling stability (3f_subsample_stability.R) and weighted full-data
# comparison (3g_weighted_vs_subsample.R).
stab <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "stability_subsample_summary.csv"))
cmp <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "stability_weighted_comparison.csv")) %>%
  mutate(diff_in_se = (weighted_estimate - subsample_mean_estimate) / subsample_mean_SE,
         weighted_sig = abs(weighted_z) > 1.96,
         subsamples_mostly_sig = prop_sig_subsamples > 0.5)
n_reps <- max(stab$n_reps)
stage_labels <- c(A_vs_real = "vs. real", B_between_model = "Models (in method)",
                  B_within_model = "Methods (in model)")
mech_labels <- c(IP = "Interpretations", EX = "Explorations")
unstable <- stab %>% filter(prop_sig_05 > 0, prop_sig_05 < 1)
stage_b <- stab %>% filter(stage != "A_vs_real")
gt2 <- cmp %>% filter(abs(diff_in_se) > 2)
n_gt2 <- nrow(gt2)
n_gt2_ex <- sum(gt2$mechanism == "EX")
n_gt2_sub_larger <- sum(abs(gt2$subsample_mean_estimate) > abs(gt2$weighted_estimate))
stab_by_stage_med <- stab %>% group_by(mechanism, stage) %>% summarise(m = median(sd_over_se), .groups = "drop") %>% pull(m)
qc_cells <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "qc_filter_and_balance.csv"))
n_synth_all <- sum(qc_cells$original_n)
n_balanced <- sum(pmin(qc_cells$original_n, qc_cells$real_count))
```

# Problem

The synthetic comments are subsampled per thread so each (model, method)
group has exactly as many comments per thread as the real group. That needs
every (thread, model, method) cell to hold *at least* as many synthetic
comments as the thread's real count. Removing length outliers *first* breaks
this: a cell can end up with fewer synthetic comments than real ones
("shortfall"), and since many cells hold a single comment, one flagged
comment can empty a cell entirely. Without any exclusion,
`r n_zero_baseline` cells fall short. Table \@ref(tab:overview) lists the six
rules compared.

```{r overview}
overview %>%
  mutate(method = unname(rule_labels[method])) %>%
  select(method, synthetic_excluded_n, synthetic_excluded_pct, shortfall_cells_n, shortfall_cells_pct) %>%
  kable(digits = c(0, 0, 2, 0, 2),
        position = "!h",
        col.names = c("Rule", "Comments excluded", "% excluded", "Cells short", "% cells short"),
        caption = "Length-outlier rules compared (detected within each model x method group; log = on log word count).")
```

# Cells that fall short, by model x method

Pooled over all groups, the rules push `r pooled_range(pooled_sf)` of cells
into shortfall (none without exclusion). The rule I would have provisionally chosen
(MAD3.5 log) reaches up to `r worst_group(sf, "pct_shortfall_cells", chosen_rule)`
in its worst group. Table \@ref(tab:shortfall) gives all groups.

```{r shortfall}
t1 <- wide_table(sf, "pct_shortfall_cells", pooled_sf)
t1 %>%
  kable(format = html_fmt(), digits = 2,
        caption = "Percent of (thread, model, method) cells with fewer synthetic comments than real ones after exclusion.") %>%
  row_spec(nrow(t1), bold = TRUE) %>% shrink()
```

# Non-zero ratings lost, by model x method and metric

Empathy labels are discrete (0 = none; > 0 = some). The tables give the
percent of each group's *non-zero-rated* synthetic comments that a rule would
exclude - i.e. how much of the informative signal is lost. Pooled over all
groups the loss ranges
`r pooled_range(pooled_nz("ER"))` for Emotional Reactions,
`r pooled_range(pooled_nz("IP"))` for Interpretations, and
`r pooled_range(pooled_nz("EX"))` for Explorations. The loss is not evenly
spread: under MAD3.5 log the worst group loses
`r worst_group(nz %>% filter(mechanism == "ER"), "pct_nonzero_excluded", chosen_rule)`,
`r worst_group(nz %>% filter(mechanism == "IP"), "pct_nonzero_excluded", chosen_rule)`, and
`r worst_group(nz %>% filter(mechanism == "EX"), "pct_nonzero_excluded", chosen_rule)`
of its non-zero ratings (Emotional Reactions, Interpretations, Explorations).
Real comments are never excluded.

```{r nz-er}
t2 <- wide_table(nz %>% filter(mechanism == "ER"), "pct_nonzero_excluded", pooled_nz("ER"))
t2 %>%
  kable(format = html_fmt(), digits = 2,
        caption = "Emotional Reactions: percent of non-zero-rated synthetic comments excluded.",
        position = "!h") %>%
  row_spec(nrow(t2), bold = TRUE) %>% shrink()
```

```{r nz-ip}
t3 <- wide_table(nz %>% filter(mechanism == "IP"), "pct_nonzero_excluded", pooled_nz("IP"))
t3 %>%
  kable(format = html_fmt(), digits = 2,
        caption = "Interpretations: percent of non-zero-rated synthetic comments excluded.",
        position = "!h") %>%
  row_spec(nrow(t3), bold = TRUE) %>% shrink()
```

```{r nz-ex}
t4 <- wide_table(nz %>% filter(mechanism == "EX"), "pct_nonzero_excluded", pooled_nz("EX"))
t4 %>%
  kable(format = html_fmt(), digits = 2,
        caption = "Explorations: percent of non-zero-rated synthetic comments excluded.",
        position = "!h") %>%
  row_spec(nrow(t4), bold = TRUE) %>% shrink()
```

# Why the Bayesian models do not need this step

1. **The outcome cannot have outliers in the usual sense.** Outlier removal
   protects against heavy-tailed *outcome* noise. Here the outcome is a
   bounded category (0/1/2, or 0/1 for Interpretations and Explorations)
   under a Bernoulli or cumulative-logit likelihood, so no single comment can
   contribute an unbounded residual. "Outlier" can only mean an unusual
   *covariate* value, comment length.
2. **Length is modeled, not ignored.** `log(length)` is a covariate in every
   model, so unusual lengths are absorbed by the length slope rather than
   distorting the group contrasts, and the log transform compresses the long
   tail so no comment gets extreme leverage. The rules above touch only
   `r sprintf("%.2f", min(overview$synthetic_excluded_pct))`% to
   `r sprintf("%.2f", max(overview$synthetic_excluded_pct))`% of synthetic
   comments, a small share of the data, which limits how much influence they can have either way.
3. **Priors and pooling limit any small set of points.** Weakly informative
   priors on all coefficients and the `post_id` random intercept's shrinkage
   toward the population mean cap how far a handful of comments can pull an
   estimate.
4. **Exclusion is not neutral.** Dropping comments on a variable associated
   with the outcome removes non-zero ratings unevenly across groups (tables
   above), which can bias exactly the group contrasts we care about. That
   cost is real, while the protection it buys is small (points 1-3).

Robustness here comes from the model's structure (bounded categorical
likelihood, length adjustment, priors), not from Bayesian inference in
general - a Gaussian model of a continuous outcome would need a robust
likelihood instead. If desired, the claim can be checked directly with a
sensitivity fit with and without the excluded comments; that is cheap for
Interpretations and Explorations, slow for Emotional Reactions.

# Per-thread subsampling is not neutral either

Keeping a random `min(n, real count)` synthetic comments per cell means the
whole analysis rests on one arbitrary draw. To see how much that matters,
the Interpretations and Explorations models (binomial `glmer` versions of the
Bayesian models, which are fast enough to repeat) were refit on `r n_reps`
independent balanced subsamples, with no outlier exclusion. Emotional
Reactions was not assessed: its ordinal fits are too slow to repeat.

Table \@ref(tab:stability) compares, for each contrast, the spread of its
estimate across subsamples (SD) with the standard error of a single fit (SE).
If the SD were small relative to the SE, the draw would not matter. Instead,
the median SD/SE is `r sprintf("%.2f", min(stab_by_stage_med))` to
`r sprintf("%.2f", max(stab_by_stage_med))` across contrast sets, and a single
draw adds up to `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * (max(stab$variance_inflation) - 1))`%
to the variance of the most affected contrast (relative to that fit's own SE).

```{r stability}
stab_tbl <- stab %>%
  group_by(mechanism, stage) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), med = median(sd_over_se), mx = max(sd_over_se),
            infl = max(variance_inflation), unst = sum(prop_sig_05 > 0 & prop_sig_05 < 1), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(mechanism = mech_labels[mechanism], stage = stage_labels[stage])
stab_tbl %>%
  kable(format = html_fmt(), digits = 2, position = "!h",
        col.names = c("Metric", "Contrast set", "N", "Median SD/SE", "Max SD/SE",
                      "Max var. infl.", "Unstable sig."),
        caption = "Spread of estimates across balanced subsamples relative to a single fit's standard error.") %>%
  shrink()
```

The headline group-vs-real contrasts never change nominal significance across
draws (`r sum(stab$stage == "A_vs_real" & stab$prop_sig_05 > 0 & stab$prop_sig_05 < 1)`
of `r sum(stab$stage == "A_vs_real")` unstable). The simple-effects contrasts
are less safe: `r nrow(unstable)` of `r nrow(stage_b)` reach nominal
significance (|z| > 1.96) in some draws but not others
(Table \@ref(tab:unstable)), so whether they look significant partly depends
on which comments happened to be kept.

```{r unstable}
unstable %>%
  arrange(mechanism, stage, desc(prop_sig_05)) %>%
  mutate(mechanism = mech_labels[mechanism], stage = stage_labels[stage],
         cond = ifelse(is.na(cond), "", ifelse(cond %in% c("dg", "sag", "sagii"), toupper(cond), str_to_title(cond))),
         prop_sig_05 = 100 * prop_sig_05) %>%
  select(mechanism, stage, cond, contrast, mean_estimate, mean_SE, prop_sig_05) %>%
  kable(format = html_fmt(), digits = 2, position = "!h",
        col.names = c("Metric", "Contrast set", "Within", "Contrast", "Mean est. (log OR)", "Mean SE", "% draws sig."),
        caption = "Simple-effects contrasts whose nominal significance depends on the subsample drawn.") %>%
  shrink()
```

## Weighting instead of subsampling

A deterministic alternative keeps *all* synthetic comments and gives each
weight `min(1, real count / cell size)` (real comments weight 1), so the
weights sum to exactly the subsampled n (`r format(n_balanced, big.mark = ",")`). The
expected subsampled log-likelihood over the random draw equals this weighted
log-likelihood, so a single weighted fit does not depend on any one draw and
uses all `r format(n_synth_all, big.mark = ",")` synthetic comments rather than
the `r format(n_balanced, big.mark = ",")` a subsample keeps. The same models
were fit with these weights and compared with the subsample results
(Table \@ref(tab:weighted)).

```{r weighted}
w_tbl <- cmp %>%
  group_by(mechanism, stage) %>%
  summarise(med_diff = median(abs(diff_in_se)), max_diff = max(abs(diff_in_se)),
            se_ratio = median(se_ratio_weighted_over_subsample),
            agree = sum(weighted_sig == subsamples_mostly_sig), n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(mechanism = mech_labels[mechanism], stage = stage_labels[stage],
         agree = sprintf("%d / %d", agree, n)) %>%
  select(-n)
w_tbl %>%
  kable(format = html_fmt(), digits = 2, position = "!h",
        col.names = c("Metric", "Contrast set", "Median |diff| (SE)", "Max |diff| (SE)",
                      "Median SE ratio", "Sig. agrees"),
        caption = "Weighted full-data fit vs. the average of the balanced subsamples: difference in estimates (in single-fit SEs), ratio of standard errors, and agreement in nominal significance.") %>%
  shrink()
```

The weighted estimates sit a median of
`r sprintf("%.2f", median(abs(cmp$diff_in_se)))` SE from the subsample average
and agree on nominal significance for `r sum(cmp$weighted_sig == cmp$subsamples_mostly_sig)`
of `r nrow(cmp)` contrasts, but they are **not** a drop-in replacement: 
`r n_gt2` contrasts differ by more than 2 SE (`r n_gt2_ex` of them Explorations),
the largest gap being `r sprintf("%.1f", max(abs(cmp$diff_in_se)))` SE. The
direction is not uniform: among those `r n_gt2`, the subsample estimate is
larger in magnitude for `r n_gt2_sub_larger`. One possible explanation is
rare-event bias inflating estimates in smaller samples (few non-zero
ratings), but this was not tested. The weighted
models' standard errors are also naive (`glmer` treats weights as precision
weights, no sandwich correction) and come out about
`r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * (median(cmp$se_ratio_weighted_over_subsample) - 1))`% larger
than a single subsample's.

## Implication

- Subsampling has a measurable effect: one random draw adds substantial
  variance and can flip the significance of borderline simple-effects
  contrasts, so a single draw should not be the primary analysis.
- Weighting all comments is a reasonable primary alternative - it is
  deterministic and uses all the data - but it is a different estimator, with
  differences of up to a few SEs from the subsample average for some
  contrasts. It should be adopted knowingly, not assumed
  equivalent.
- A weighted Bayesian fit would need its own check (`brms` weights give a
  pseudo-likelihood, so its posterior widths are approximate) and, for
  Emotional Reactions, could not be verified against repeated subsamples.
  Reporting both a weighted primary fit and a subsample sensitivity check on
  the cheaper mechanisms would make the choice transparent.
